rows.description: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` exists and defines jobs running `bun typecheck`, `bun lint`, and `bun test` triggered on both `push` and `pull_request` events
rows.verifyMethod: `cat .github/workflows/ci.yml` and confirm all three commands and both triggers are present

rows.description: README.md contains a GitHub Actions badge linking to the CI workflow for `[user]/ai-assistant` that renders as passing
rows.verifyMethod: `grep -i "github.com/[user]/ai-assistant/actions" README.md` and visit the badge URL to confirm green status

rows.description: `docs/adr/` contains exactly 5 ADR files covering: JSONL-vs-database, hooks-vs-middleware, SKILL.md discovery, Bun-vs-Node, and prompt injection defense; each file is 300–500 words
rows.verifyMethod: `ls docs/adr/ | wc -l` equals 5; `wc -w docs/adr/*.md` shows each file between ~250–550 words (accounting for markdown overhead)

rows.description: Each ADR follows a consistent structure including a Context, Decision, and Consequences section (or equivalent named headers)

Architecture diagram file exists as PNG or SVG in the repo (e.g., `docs/architecture.png` or `docs/architecture.svg`) and depicts all 8 lifecycle stages: user input → hooks → context router → skill dispatch → tool execution → post-tool hooks → output validator → memory capture
rows.verifyMethod: `ls docs/architecture.*` returns a `.png` or `.svg`; open file and manually confirm all 8 labeled nodes are present and connected in sequence

rows.description: README.md references or embeds the architecture diagram PNG/SVG, either replacing or supplementing the existing Mermaid diagram
`CONTRIBUTING.md` exists at repo root and contains distinct sections for: adding a skill, writing a hook, running tests, code style, and PR process
rows.verifyMethod: `cat CONTRIBUTING.md` and confirm five headings covering each topic are present

rows.description: `CONTRIBUTING.md` includes the exact `bun test` command (or equivalent) so contributors can run the test suite locally without additional research
At least 3 and no more than 5 open GitHub Issues on `[user]/ai-assistant` are labeled `good-first-issue`
rows.verifyMethod: `gh issue list --label good-first-issue --repo [user]/ai-assistant` returns 3–5 open issues

rows.description: Git log shows individual commits per logical unit of work (CI setup, each ADR, diagram, CONTRIBUTING.md) rather than a single bulk commit
rows.verifyMethod: `git log --oneline` shows ≥7 distinct commits with messages corresponding to each deliverable component
